channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: Mexican cartel leader on FBI's 10 most wanted fugitive list arrested
item.description: Fausto Isidro Meza-Flores, known as "Chapo Isidro," was captured in an operation in Sinaloa.

item.title: Storms expected on both coasts threatens Thanksgiving travel
item.description: The mayor of San Francisco is asking people in the city not to travel unless "absolutely essential." Meanwhile, a storm moving up the Eastern seaboard could also cause travel delays ahead of Thanksgiving. (Image credit: Joe Raedle)

item.title: Mexico detains top cartel boss 'El Chapo Isidro,' setting off violence
item.description: Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, better known as "El Chapo Isidro," was one of the FBI's most wanted fugitives. His arrest in northwest Mexico on Saturday has sparked violence in the region. (Image credit: Claudia Rosel)

item.title: Drone attack sets Russian cargo ship ablaze in Gulf of Finland
item.description: A Russian cargo ship caught fire after ​being hit by drones in the Baltic Sea on Saturday and drifted into Finnish waters. Reporting from Kyiv, FRANCE 24's Gulliver Cragg notes that the ship is affiliated with a major Russian military logistics company. While Ukrainian authorities typically neither confirm nor deny responsibility, analysts cite a clear motive for the targeting, Cragg explains.

item.title: COP31: Deep divisions persist over energy, finance and science
item.description: COP31 climate talks in Turkey have gone into overtime, with deep divisions over fossil fuels, climate finance and global warming targets delaying an agreement. A revised draft dropped all mention of fossil fuels, prompting strong criticism from the EU and a dozen countries demanding a clear commitment to phase them out. Negotiators are also split over a proposed global electrification target, carbon capture and the future of UN climate science reports. Developing nations have voiced anger over the removal of a $120 billion climate adaptation funding target. Australia is now racing to secure a revised deal before delegates leave. France 24 journalist Adria Rocha Cutiller tells us the latest.

item.title: FBI criminal database hacked
item.description: The FBI is investigating a reported major cyberattack targeting its national law enforcement database, the National Crime Information Center (NCIC), which holds sensitive criminal justice records, including information on fugitives, missing persons, criminal histories and stolen property. President Donald Trump said he had just been briefed on the incident, describing it as “not good”. FRANCE 24’s Fraser Jackson reports from Washington DC.

item.title: Man convicted of starting palisades fire
item.description: A Los Angeles County jury found former rideshare driver Jonathan Rinderknecht guilty on Friday of starting the 2025 Palisades fire, which caused widespread destruction and loss of life. He faces a prison sentence of between five and 40 years. Liza Kaminov has more.

item.title: French police officers convicted of racist assault
item.description: A French court on Friday sentenced three policemen to serve time over the beating of a black music producer in 2020. It also recognized the assault on Michelle Zecler was racially motivated.

item.title: Endurance athlete swims in Hormuz Strait
item.description: The Strait of Hormuz remains largely blocked, with Iran attacking vessels attempting to cross it. As concerns grow over the environmental impact of the war, with toxic chemicals spreading through the air and sea, one swimmer and ocean advocate has gone a step further than issuing warnings: he plunged into the polluted and dangerous waters of the strait, calling on all sides to end the conflict.

item.title: France: Demonstrations losing steam as movement enters sixth week
item.description: Around 2,200 people took part in protests across France by 2pm local time, according to the Interior Ministry, which recorded 44 demonstrations nationwide and seven arrests, with the situation described as generally calm. Turnout was lower than on previous Saturdays. Reporting from Place de la République in Paris, FRANCE 24’s Antonia Kerrigan said rent rights organisations had also joined the sixth consecutive Saturday of protests, highlighting their growing pan-European dimension, with demonstrations taking place in seven European countries, including Spain, Portugal, Greece and Germany, where rising living costs and access to affordable housing are among the main concerns.

item.title: Countries race to secure Cop31 deal
item.description: COP31 climate talks have overrun their schedule as countries race to agree on a new global climate deal, following criticism of an earlier draft that made no mention of fossil fuels. The EU has warned that the current proposal risks turning the summit into a “fossil fuel summit”, as negotiators work towards a revised, potentially final agreement expected later today. France 24 International affairs editor Jamie Smith-Maillet tells us more.

item.title: New day of protests across France
item.description: France faces a sixth consecutive Saturday of protests, with demonstrators taking to the streets to rally over the rising cost of living and the government's handling of weeks of social unrest ahead of next year's presidential election. France 24 journalist Antonia Kerrigan tells us more.

item.title: What's behind the uptick in attacks in the Strait of Hormuz?
item.description: Reported Strait of Hormuz attacks have been higher in number in October and November than other months since the war between the U.S., Israel and Iran began, data shows.

item.title: Killer robots: U.N. talks fall short of hopes for legally binding rules
item.description: U.N. talks in Geneva have failed to deliver binding rules on autonomous weapons, as humanitarian groups warn that military AI is advancing far faster than diplomacy. (Image credit: Efrem Lukatsky)

item.title: Federal jury convicts man of starting the deadly 2025 Palisades Fire in Los Angeles
item.description: Prosecutors argued the defendant, 30-year-old Jonathan Rinderknecht, had been "mad at everything" in the days leading up to the January 2025 fire, which killed 12 people. (Image credit: Etienne Laurent)

item.title: Suspected cartel leader 'El Chapo Isidro' from FBI most-wanted list captured in Mexico
item.description: Suspected cartel leader Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as El Chapo Isidro, has been captured.

item.title: Perspective: Defining 'human'
item.description: The Cambridge Dictionary has chosen the word "human" as its Word of the Year. Why ever might a word that entered the English language over 500 years ago be so honored? (Image credit: Andreea Alexandru)

item.title: Cargo ship runs aground off French coast
item.description: A Maltese-flagged cargo ship remains stranded off the coast of south-western France after running aground. French authorities are preparing an operation to prevent the vessel from capsizing and potentially causing pollution. The ship was not carrying any cargo, and all 19 crew members were safely evacuated by helicopter. Dan Quinlan reports.

item.title: Russia tests NATO’s eastern defences
item.description: Two Russian missiles and a suspected drone came down in Poland on Friday in what Prime Minister Donald Tusk said was likely an "intentional provocation" timed to coincide with European military exercises in the country for a possible postwar mission in Ukraine. Senior Lecturer in Conflict and Security at King's College in London, Domitilla Sagramoso, shares further insights.

item.title: Thousands protest overs prices, education, military spending in France and Europe
item.description: France is bracing for a sixth consecutive Saturday of protests, with demonstrators expected to rally over the rising cost of living and the government's handling of weeks of social unrest ahead of next year's presidential election. France 24 journalist Antonia Kerrigan tells us the latest from Paris.

item.title: Anthropic worker claims to have solved a Holy Grail of math problems with the help of AI
item.description: A mathematician who works for artificial intelligence giant Anthropic claims he has solved a Holy Grail of math problems with the help of the company's AI tool Claude. It marks the second time in recent months that an AI company or someone linked to one claims to have cracked a famed unsolved math problem. (Image credit: Seth Wenig)

item.title: Ethiopia: Tackling period poverty and stigma
item.description: In Ethiopia, entrepreneur Hanan Ahmed is tackling period poverty and the stigma surrounding menstruation. By producing affordable reusable sanitary pads and raising awareness in schools, she hopes to make menstrual health more accessible and help girls stay in class. Report by Awa Diouf & Guillaume Gougeon.

item.title: Ethiopia - Eritrea: Troops mobilise along the border
item.description: More than 200 former Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) fighters surrendered to Ethiopia’s federal military Friday, state-affiliated media reported, amid escalating border tensions with neighboring Eritrea. France 24 correspondent Tom Canetti tells us the latest.

item.title: Music strikes a chord at French protest
item.description: Throughout history, protest songs have brought people together across genres, rallying against war, racism, inequality and the establishment. Music is also playing a key role in the youth-led demonstrations here in France. Our reporters went to meet some of the musicians using their voices to express the protesters’ demands.

item.title: 'Accept cookies'? Russia collects data from swaths of unknowing Swedes
item.description: A Russian tech firm backed by an oligarch close to President Vladimir Putin has secretly been collecting data from hundreds of thousands – possibly millions – of Swedes, a newspaper investigation found. The revelation has rattled the Nordic nation, whose proximity to Russia and unusually open public records system make it particularly vulnerable to Moscow’s hybrid war tactics.

item.title: 'Unacceptable': EU chief condemns alleged Russian plot to kill US-Ukrainian citizen
item.description: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen condemned an alleged Russian intelligence plot to assassinate a US-Ukrainian citizen in Denmark, vowing full solidarity with Copenhagen.

item.title: Was Vladimir Putin 'snubbed' by Xi Jinping? Viral handshake video is AI fake
item.description: A viral video appearing to show China's Xi Jinping "snubbing" Vladimir Putin at the APEC summit has racked up millions of views, fuelling speculation about tensions between Beijing and Moscow. But the footage is fake. FRANCE 24 traced the original video to an earlier summit, where the two leaders did shake hands. The creator, who runs a satire account, admitted to manipulating the footage using Grok Imagine, an AI tool developed by Elon Musk's xAI, as Vedika Bahl explains.

item.title: Man charged with attempted murder after councillor stabbed in Bradford
item.description: A man has been charged with attempted murder after a councillor was stabbed while out door-knocking in Bradford.

item.title: 5 ways to turn off your 'work brain' after the day ends
item.description: Don't let your work troubles follow you home. Psychologist Guy Winch shares techniques to help you stop ruminating about your nine-to-five, so you can focus on what really matters. (Image credit: Beck Harlan for NPR)

item.title: An effort to circumvent the Electoral College may be within reach. But hurdles remain
item.description: A national effort to ensure that only winners of the popular vote become president could reach a critical milestone soon. (Image credit: Mark Felix)

item.title: Anthropic says it will put humanity first. Will its IPO change that?
item.description: Critics say now that the AI giant is a public company, its commitment to put safety ahead of commercial success will be tested. (Image credit: Michael M. Santiago)

item.title: Denmark accuses Russia of assassination plot, expels diplomat
item.description: Denmark has accused Moscow of being behind a failed assassination attempt targeting a Ukrainian-American rapper in Copenhagen, further escalating tensions between Europe and Russia. In response, Danish authorities have ordered the expulsion of a Russian diplomat and announced tighter restrictions on visas for Russian tourists. Yuka Royer reports.

item.title: Houthis launch strikes on Saudi Arabia
item.description: Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen continue to exchange strikes with the Saudi-led coalition. The coalition said it intercepted and destroyed three ballistic missiles fired towards Riyadh early on Saturday. It marks the second Houthi attack on the Saudi capital in recent days, following Saudi-led strikes on Houthi targets in Yemen. Yuka Royer has the latest.

item.title: Russian projectiles hit Poland as NATO tensions rise
item.description: Three Russian projectiles came down in Poland on Friday, prompting NATO to condemn what it called a grave violation of Polish airspace. A suspected jet-powered drone and a missile struck separate locations near the Ukrainian border, while another missile crashed just 35 kilometres from an area where European troops are taking part in military exercises. Meanwhile, troops from eight NATO countries are conducting drills in neighbouring Lithuania. With US-led peace talks yet to make a breakthrough, tensions between Europe and Russia remain high. Peter O’Brien reports.

item.title: Nations League: France to face Spain in quarter-finals, England to take on Norway
item.description: A chance for revenge. Beaten by Spain in the World Cup semi-finals last July, France will meet La Roja again in the Nations League quarter-finals next March.

item.title: EU, UK reach reset deal after Brexit
item.description: The UK and the EU signed three agreements on Friday at a summit in Brussels, marking a new effort to reset post-Brexit relations. The deals aim to reduce red tape for food exports, link emissions trading schemes and allow tens of thousands of young people to live and work more freely across the Channel. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has called Brexit an “obvious failure” to deliver on its promises and wants to deepen ties with the EU, a position criticised by veteran Brexiteer Nigel Farage, who has warned of a political backlash. Daniel Quinlan has this story.

item.title: German bidder stages last-gasp bid to rescue Poundland
item.description: A German investment firm has made a last-minute entry into the race to save Poundland, just days before its directors face the bleak prospect of appointing administrators to one of Britain's biggest high street retailers.

item.title: Ladbrokes-owner Entain in talks with CVC after gambling tax hit
item.description: The London-listed owner of Ladbrokes and Coral is in talks to sell part of its business to one of the world's biggest private equity firms as it tries to mitigate the impact of Labour's latest tax raid on the gambling industry.

item.title: Denmark says it thwarted 'Russian plot' to kill US-Ukrainian rapper
item.description: Police thwarted a Russian plot to kill a US-Ukrainian rapper who was performing in Denmark, according to authorities.

item.description: The Naval Criminal Investigative Service says it is investigating a famed Marine Corps veteran over undisclosed allegations

item.title: Harry Kane shares image from hospital bed after injury
item.description: England captain Harry Kane has vowed to be back for the "business end of the season" after undergoing surgery on a torn ligament in his left ankle.

item.description: The Trump administration tried to step in after Kalshi warned it could be crippled if a judge grants a temporary restraining order being sought by the New York AG.

item.description: A cold weather warning has been extended as temperatures dropped to -10C (14F) overnight into Saturday.

item.description: A Lancet Psychiatry report calls problematic internet use a global health concern, affecting more than 1 in 10 people. ABC News’ Dr. Jennifer Miao explains the impact and how to protect yourself.

item.description: A New York Times reporter went undercover as a porch pirate to help identify the best ways to keep your home and packages safe as package deliveries ramp up this holiday season.

item.description: White House National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross has been fired, according to a source close to the White House.

item.description: A top House Democrat is investigating the use of encrypted messaging apps by Justice Department employees to communicate official business

item.title: Anthropic among big fallers in global stock market rout
item.description: Shares in Anthropic have fallen by more than 10% at Friday's open on Wall Street, just a day after their record-breaking Nasdaq debut, as part of a global stock market rout.

item.title: WATCH: Riverboat captain celebrates more than 50 years on the Mississippi River
item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to riverboat captain Robbie Mitchell, who is marking a major milestone aboard the legendary steamboat Natchez.

item.title: WATCH: New video angle shows moment of Brooklyn apartment building's deadly collapse
item.description: Dash cam video from a bus passing by shows the terrifying moment a three-story Brooklyn apartment building buckled and crumbled to the ground, killing eight people and injuring multiple others.

item.title: Myanmar rejects UN court's genocide ruling as 'unfair'
item.description: Myanmar branded a ruling by the UN's highest court that its security forces conducted state-sponsored genocide against Rohingya Muslims as "unfair".

item.title: WATCH: Grand Theft Auto VI is back and shattering records
item.description: The excitement around the release of GTA VI is causing gamers to “call out sick” to play and has lit up Miami in Vice City colors. ABC News’ Ashan Singh dives into what the hype is all about.

item.title: Trump China trip: Iran and Ukraine not in 'peace declaration' and more takeaways
item.description: Trump heads back to Washington after meeting with Xi and Putin -- the first sitdown between the three superpowers -- with no tangible diplomatic breakthroughs in hand.

item.description: There are three other former soldiers who are on the military’s death row.

item.description: Thomas Markle is fit to stand trial on charges of possessing child sexual abuse material, a US court has ruled.

item.description: The UK is conducting offensive cyber operations against Russia, China, Iran and North Korea, a top military commander has for the first time revealed.

item.title: What Obama said to newly elected Democrats after midterm gains
item.description: Former President Barack Obama told Democratic U.S. House members-elect on Wednesday that they should value their ideological diversity even if they have disagreements.

item.title: Xi tells Trump US must do 'the right thing' over Taiwan to avoid 'great turbulence'
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping used his meeting with President Donald Trump in Shenzhen on Thursday to warn against the creation of "turbulence" over the issue of Taiwan.

item.title: WATCH: Trump calls Putin, Xi his friends after meeting
item.description: Doug Lute, former U.S. ambassador to NATO, says President Donald Trump referring to Putin and Xi as friends is "concerning for America's allies."

item.description: Actor Kel Mitchell shares how he's using his star power to help families in need.

item.description: "GMA" sponsor Chevrolet teams up with rising country star Zach Top to surprise a military family.
